stories.headline: GORE ASKS PUBLIC FOR PATIENCE; BUSH STARTS TRANSITION MOVES; ADMINISTRATION WITHHOLDS AID
stories.summary: Gov George W Bush presses forward with transition plans while Vice Pres Al Gore pleads in nationwide address for public patience while he contests award of Florida's 25 decisive electoral votes to Bush; Gore says he is not engaged in struggle for power, but in effort to preserve democracy itself; says challenge is to ensure that every American has change to register choice in one closest presidential races in American history; says fair count of Florida vote would provide him with more than enough votes to defeat Bush; blames series of lawsuits by Republicans and 'organized intimidation' of local canvassing officials for delay in reaching full count; Bush running mate and transition director Dick Cheney sharply criticizes Gore and White House for refusing to authorize public money and government office space for Bush transition; says administration has duty to honor certified results of Florida election; says Gore's obstinacy is getting in way of peaceful transfer of power; Florida Gov Jeb Bush signs document officially certifying brother as winner of state's 25 electoral votes; senior Republicans in Congress begin referring to Bush as president-elect; photos (M)

stories.headline: Will Nasdaq's Fall Haunt the Democrats?
stories.summary: Gretchen Morgenson column on negative impact of falling Nasdaq stock prices on Vice Pres Al Gore's presidential campaign; notes analysts expect Gore victory would do little for stock prices, while victory by Gov George W Bush would likely boost prices; graph of drop in Nasdaq stocks (M)

stories.headline: Entering Last Act, Senate Rivals Stick to the Script; Mrs. Clinton Preaches to the Party Faithful
stories.summary: Hillary Rodham Clinton moves to close out campaign for US Senate from New York by urging black parishioners in New York City to support her; makes appearances at seven churches in seven-hour period; implores churchgoers to vote Democratic, linking herself to husband and Vice Pres Al Gore at every turn; photos (M)
